title: Watch (Mark 13)
hookLine: the Temple will fall, no one knows the hour, so watch
carry: finish today as if it matters

cards: Master, look at these stones! Look at these buildings! Men from Galilee are walking out of the Temple in the big city, and one disciple can't help himself.

Jesus looks and says every stone will be thrown down. Then he climbs the Mount of Olives, sits facing the Temple, and four disciples ask him quietly: when? What follows is a long answer, the whole of chapter thirteen.

teach.h: NOT A STONE UPON A STONE.
teach.b: First, the stones. In the Douay-Rheims: "There shall not be left a stone upon a stone, that shall not be thrown down." History records that Roman armies later destroyed the Temple, after a revolt.
For Mark's first readers, that may have been recent memory, or still to come.
Second, the troubles: wars and rumors of wars, earthquakes, famines, false messiahs, families divided, persecution. Hard to hear. But he keeps saying: don't be alarmed.
The end is not yet. Hold on.

teach.h: NO ONE KNOWS THE DAY OR HOUR.
teach.b: Third, the surprise: "But of that day or hour no man knoweth, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father." Not the angels. Not even the Son.

Christians have wrestled with what it means that the Son doesn't know; the Church reads it in light of his true humanity, and of what was his to reveal. What the verse plainly does is leave no room for a date.
A man goes on a journey and tells the doorkeeper to stay awake, because the master might come back in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.
Some readers notice those four times return in the next chapters: the supper in the evening, the garden at night, Peter at cockcrow, Pilate in the morning.

teach.h: WHAT I SAY TO YOU, I SAY TO ALL: WATCH.
teach.b: And the speech's last line: "And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch." This week in Mark: the children, the rich man, Bartimaeus, the fig tree, Caesar's coin, the widow. And now, one word for everyone.

how: Catholics hear Jesus's call to watch at the start of Advent each year, and profess in the Creed that Christ will come again, while the Church teaches that no one can know the day or the hour.

look for signs to work out the date

games.q: you're one of the four on the Mount of Olives. you ask Jesus when it will all happen. what does he finally say?
o: no one knows the day or hour, so watch.
it will happen before the week is out.
games.why: no one knows, not the angels, not the Son, but the Father. and the last word: "Watch."

practice: Watching doesn't mean staring at the sky or reading the news in a panic; it means being awake to what's in front of you.
Think through the rest of today and find one unfinished thing you've been putting off, or one person you haven't really paid attention to, and choose to finish it, or face them, before you sleep.
If you pray, you can offer the rest of the day.

wordCard.voice: Watch. The last word of Jesus's speech on the Mount of Olives: stay awake, because no one knows the hour. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: stay awake, keep watch. the last word of the speech.

carryVoice: Your line: finish today as if it matters. Awake, not on autopilot. See you tomorrow.
